issues.legal_issue: An implemented consent decree recording a family settlement cannot be reopened merely to relitigate whether the settled properties were joint family or self-acquired property.
material_facts: The family members treated the properties as joint family property in an earlier partition suit and agreed to divide them through a settlement recorded in a consent decree.
The parties acted on the decree, including by dividing property and completing subsequent transactions.
The challenge to the settlement rested on alleged fraud that was not established.
issues.conclusion: The consent decree and the family settlement could not be reopened on the basis that the properties were self-acquired rather than joint family property.
issues.legal_principle: A family arrangement made to preserve peace and harmony may involve give and take, and an implemented settlement is not lightly disturbed. The Court relied on Mst. Rukhmabai v. Lala Laxminarayan, Hari Shankar Singhania v. Gaur Hari Singhania, Ramdev Food Products (P) Ltd. v. Arvindbhai Rambhai Patel, and Ram Charan Das v. Girjanandini Devi. Fraud may vitiate a consent decree, but it must be pleaded and proved.

rule.if: family_partition_dispute and settlement_recorded_in_consent_decree and consent_decree_implemented and not fraud_on_settlement_proved

predicates.family_partition_dispute: The proceeding concerns the division of property among members of a family.
predicates.settlement_recorded_in_consent_decree: The family members agreed to a property settlement that was recorded in a consent decree.
predicates.consent_decree_implemented: The parties acted on the consent decree by carrying out the agreed division or related transactions.
predicates.fraud_on_settlement_proved: The party challenging the settlement proved that fraud affected the settlement or the decree.

issues.definition: When a family property settlement has been recorded in a consent decree and acted upon, the decree cannot be reopened on the basis of property classification unless fraud affecting it is proved.

issues.legal_issue: A party alleging fraud or misrepresentation to avoid a registered instrument must plead and prove the particulars of the alleged wrongdoing, and a voidable instrument must be set aside.
material_facts: The challenged deeds and powers of attorney were registered or executed before advocates or a registering officer.
The challengers acknowledged signing documents and had evidence indicating awareness of the documents' character.
The pleadings alleged generally that signatures had been obtained through misrepresentation but did not state the particulars of the alleged fraud.
The evidence did not establish that the documents' character had been misrepresented.
issues.conclusion: Fraud was not proved; the instruments were not void ab initio and had to be set aside to be avoided.
issues.legal_principle: Order VI Rule 4 of the Code of Civil Procedure requires particulars of fraud or misrepresentation to be pleaded. Under Section 16 of the Indian Contract Act, a transaction induced by undue influence, misrepresentation, or fraud is voidable. A registered document is presumed to have been validly executed, and the challenger bears the burden of rebutting that presumption. The Court relied on Prem Singh v. Birbal, A.C. Ananthaswamy v. Boraiah, Mst. Rukhmabai v. Lala Laxminarayan, Chief Engineer, M.S.E.B. v. Suresh Raghunath Bhokare, Ramesh B. Desai v. Bipin Vadilal Mehta, and Sangramsinh P. Gaekwad v. Shantadevi P. Gaekwad.

rule.if: civil_challenge_to_registered_instrument and fraud_or_misrepresentation_alleged and fraud_particulars_not_pleaded and execution_or_document_character_acknowledged

predicates.civil_challenge_to_registered_instrument: A party in a civil proceeding challenges a registered instrument as having been procured improperly.
predicates.fraud_or_misrepresentation_alleged: The challenger alleges that another person procured the instrument by fraud or misrepresentation.
predicates.fraud_particulars_not_pleaded: The challenger does not plead specific details of the alleged false representation or other wrongdoing.
predicates.execution_or_document_character_acknowle: The challenger acknowledges signing the document or facts show awareness of its character.

issues.definition: In a civil challenge to a registered instrument, a general allegation of fraud without particulars, alongside acknowledged execution or awareness of the document's character, does not establish fraud, and a voidable instrument must be set aside.

issues.legal_issue: A family member's relinquishment of property rights is not invalid solely because the instrument provides no adequate monetary consideration.
material_facts: The sisters executed a written and registered family partition instrument relinquishing their interests in favour of close family members.
The instrument stated only nominal consideration, and the evidence showed affection and trust within the family.
The contention that the relinquishment was invalid for want of consideration was not pleaded and supported by evidence at trial.
issues.conclusion: The relinquishment was not invalidated for want of adequate consideration, and the challenge based on that ground could not be raised for the first time at the appellate stage.
issues.legal_principle: Section 25 of the Indian Contract Act recognizes exceptions to the rule that an agreement without consideration is void, including written and registered agreements and agreements made on account of natural love and affection. A relinquishment may be made with or without consideration, and a registered instrument may operate as a gift if it manifests the required intention. The Court relied on Sections 2(d) and 25 of the Indian Contract Act, Sections 122 and 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, and Kuppuswamy Chettiar v. A.S.P.A. Arumugam Chettiar. Whether an agreement falls within an exception may depend on facts and must be properly raised and supported by evidence.

rule.if: challenge_to_family_relinquishment and written_and_registered_instrument and close_family_relationship and consideration_objection_not_properly_pleaded

predicates.challenge_to_family_relinquishment: A party challenges a relinquishment of property rights made as part of a family division.
predicates.written_and_registered_instrument: The relinquishment is contained in a written instrument that is registered.
predicates.close_family_relationship: The persons giving up and receiving the property rights are close family members.
predicates.consideration_objection_not_properly_ple: The contention that the relinquishment lacked legally sufficient consideration was not properly raised and supported in the trial proceeding.

issues.definition: A family relinquishment in a written and registered instrument between close relatives is not invalidated for lack of adequate consideration where the consideration objection was not properly pleaded.

issues.legal_issue: A suit seeking to avoid a voidable partition deed must be brought within the limitation period running from when the facts entitling the plaintiff to avoid it became known.
material_facts: The suit sought partition despite an earlier partition deed that the Court found was voidable rather than void ab initio.
The challengers had knowledge of the partition deed before bringing suit, as shown by documents and transactions recognizing or acting on it.
The suit was brought after the applicable limitation period had elapsed from that knowledge.
issues.conclusion: The suit was barred by limitation because the voidable partition deed had not been set aside within the applicable period.
issues.legal_principle: Article 59 of the Schedule to the Limitation Act applies to a suit to cancel or set aside an instrument and runs from when the relevant facts first become known to the plaintiff. Section 31 of the Specific Relief Act provides for relief setting aside an instrument. The Court relied on Prem Singh v. Birbal, M/s. Bay Berry Apartments Pvt. Ltd. v. Shobha, and Utha Moidu Haji v. Kuningarath Kunhabdulla.

predicates.suit_to_partition_challenging_voidable_d: The proceeding seeks partition while challenging a deed that is voidable rather than void ab initio.
predicates.plaintiff_knew_facts_entitling_avoidance: The plaintiff knew the facts that entitled the plaintiff to seek avoidance of the deed.
predicates.suit_filed_after_limitation_period: The plaintiff filed the suit after the applicable limitation period had elapsed from that knowledge.

issues.definition: A suit seeking partition while challenging a voidable deed is barred when the plaintiff knew the grounds for avoiding the deed and filed after the applicable limitation period.
